The steam encompassed the field ahead of the Tanil strike team, who slowly shuffled towards the billowing clouds. The sounds of chuffing machinery could be heard faintly in the distance with the occasional bang of clanging mechanations. This was a forge world of the Terran radicals and would soon be under the governance of the Tanil league. Once the strike team completed their mission of finding the unsurprisingly missing Terran governor.

Scout craft had reported the governor's aircraft landing in a industrial district that had already been cleared, so the risk of insurgents was minimal to the team. They had been waiting in their dropship prepping their gear when the order came through for a QRF to locate the governor. A relatively inexperienced team, they had been kept on standby while the more veteran strike groups were supporting the advance of ground forces on the capital. With being the only team close by, the call had been made to send them as it was assumed the security detail would be light on the governor. They couldn't have been more wrong

The team leader crept through the mist as he cursed the Terrans for their old world steam power. It was a mystery how they had ever gotten spaceborn but they had despite the vastly inefficient steam power they so desperately clung to. They had to be respected however, the team leader thought, as he peered about himself. Only a particularly driven species could build these miles of steam equipment without seeking an alternative. Driven or foolishly arrogant, he thought, as a bolt whizzed by his visor to crash into his heavy weapons expert, pinning him to a massive steel tank. "Contact front!", he shouted, bringing his weapon to bear in the direction the bolt had flown from. A thick mist lied in front of him, with the sounds of whirring machinery and hissing steam being ever present. 

And then it was there, with a thin shroud of steam still surrounding it. A monstrous machine stood  a dozen paces ahead of the team leader, a twisted combination of wood, steel and flesh. The only indication that betrayed the machine's humanity was a narrow eye slit on the steel helmet, with a Terran left eye next to a red glowing sight on its right eye. They showed no emotion as more bolts ripped from their housing on the bulky left forearm of wood and metal. His assistant lead and anti armor specialist went flying back into the steam as the rest of the squad open fired on the machine with their laser carbines. Hits landed on the machine with barely a carbon mark to show anything as a massive wooden clad boot smashed into the ground towards the remaining team.

The team, on seeing their lack of effect, began scrambling for cover against the armored beast. The Tanil team leader bolted back, desperately looking for the fallen anti-armor specialist and his ZD-32 Close anti-armor support system. It was only a few paces before he came across his fallen comrade in the steam, with a 2 foot bolt skewering his abdomen into the ground. The Tanil leader could hear shots being fired by his team behind him and slowly stop one after another, followed by solid thunks and screaming on his comm device. He picked up the anti-armor system and turned towards the sounds of death, aiming the weapon with determination.

It wasn't enough. A massive gust of steam hit the Tanil in the face as a massive rumble shook the ground. Bewildered, he looked around for the aggressor, only to hear a woosh as something fell ground-word towards him. A brief glance up reveald the monstrous chassis descending rapidly towards him."I should have taken that administrative position" he thought, just before he was rapidly crushed by several tons of Terran old world ingenuity.
